correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 and positive generalist rates and weights, the fixed-budget weighted miss loss has a strictly positive second derivative due to at least one nonspecialist species. The unique minimum includes positive specialist effort if and only if the zero-effort derivative is negative. For specialist rate above target generalist rate, this derivative equals a positive exponential factor times H, and H has nonnegative second derivative with only constant or strictly convex possibilities. Its strict negative set is an interval, hence at most two transitions. The two-species case reduces to a monotone single exponential minus a constant. The stated three-pest witness has exact quadratic roots and positive far-end derivative, proving a strict interior mixture only between the roots. The standalone checker passed 32550 supplementary assertions; these are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The surveyed published multi-pest/multi-trap literature supplies the practical motivation and a broader numerical optimization model, but not a theorem classifying the activation set of a single-target specialist over all fixed budgets. The claim is only the exact specialist-activation interval and sharp three-pest on/off/on-generalist counterexample. It is not a claim to have invented convexity, Poisson failure laws, or mixture optimization. No published record checked implies both the arbitrary-m interval bound and its sharp three-species pure-to-mixed-to-pure witness under the same conditions. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The full text of Kompas et al. (2019) was not accessed; its abstract alone cannot exclude mathematically equivalent subcases in its proofs.
Classical constrained convex optimization and exponential-function theory are broad enough that an unlocated equivalent formulation in older resource-allocation research is possible.
The statement concerns a specific Poisson weighted-miss objective and is not asserted to follow from or predict a field-calibrated optimal surveillance policy.

value.rationale: The question of whether an expensive single-target detection tool should be retained when a multi-pest monitoring budget grows is a naturally motivated surveillance design issue. The new structural statement gives a universal connected-support law for a specialist over arbitrarily many pest classes, with a sharp three-pest minimal configuration in which the specialist enters an optimal mixture and is later eliminated. This invalidates a plausible nesting heuristic; the exact rate/weight witness and two computable thresholds provide a controlled test case. Neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a simple restatement of the numerical optimization in the motivating paper, it does not claim a calibrated field benefit or significance measured by raw detection gain.
